notes.meaning: About two years after his first visions, God gave a new message to Zechariah. The temple in Jerusalem was being rebuilt and was about half finished. God spoke to the prophet in late autumn, during the month of Chislev.

A delegation led by Sharezer and Regem-melech came to Jerusalem with their men. They came to the temple site to pray and seek the favor of the Lord. They wanted guidance on an important religious question.

The messengers asked the priests and prophets whether they should keep fasting in the fifth month, as they had done for seventy years. That annual fast had mourned the burning of the temple by the Babylonians. Now that the new temple was rising, they wondered if that sorrowful fast was still needed.
The Lord of Hosts spoke directly to Zechariah with the answer. The prophet did not give his own human opinion, but delivered the exact word of God to the people.

God told Zechariah to address the entire nation and all the priests, not just the messengers. For seventy years they had fasted to mourn the fallen temple and their slain governor, Gedaliah. Yet God asked whether they were truly seeking Him, or merely feeling sorry for their own losses.

When the people sat down to eat and drink at feasts, they did it entirely to please themselves. Selfish desire was at the center of their feasting just as it was in their fasting. Outward religious habits mean nothing to God when the heart is focused only on self.

God pointed them back to the messages He gave through earlier prophets before the exile. In those days, Jerusalem and the surrounding plains and foothills were secure, crowded, and fruitful. If the people had obeyed God back then, the temple would never have burned and the fasts would never have been needed.
The Lord spoke to Zechariah again to explain what He truly wanted from His people. He repeated the moral duties that previous generations had neglected.

The Lord commanded the people to act with honest justice and show loyal love and mercy to one another. Real obedience to God shows itself in how people treat their neighbors every day. True kindness pleases God far more than going without food on a fast day.

God gave strict orders not to mistreat the most helpless people, including widows, orphans, foreigners, and the poor. He also commanded them not to plot or harbor cruel thoughts against one another. God's law searches both outward actions and the secret attitudes of the heart.

The older generations had flatly refused to listen to God. They pulled away like a stubborn ox refusing to wear a wooden yoke. They covered their ears on purpose so they would not have to hear His voice.

The people hardened their hearts until they were like flint or diamond, refusing to soften under God's words. They ignored the law and the warnings that the Holy Spirit spoke through the earlier prophets. Because of this willful rebellion, the Lord of Hosts poured out His great anger upon them.

God had called out to them to turn back, but they would not pay attention. Therefore, when disaster struck and they cried out for rescue, God refused to listen to their prayers. When people deliberately turn away from God's commands, they close the door to His help.

God drove the rebellious people into exile among unfamiliar nations, like chaff blown away by a whirlwind. The lovely, fruitful land of promise was left empty and ruined, with no travelers passing through. Their own stubborn sin, not just the invading armies, caused the ruin of their homeland.
